avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates antiplatelet effects; increases bleeding risk through platelet inhibition and von Willebrand factor reduction
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue ginkgo biloba; counsel patient on bleeding precautions and signs of hemorrhage

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Enhances antiplatelet aggregation effects; increases risk of clinically significant bleeding
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose garlic supplements; dietary garlic is acceptable in normal amounts

avoid_supplements.name: Ginger (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates platelet inhibition and anticoagulant effects; increases bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid therapeutic doses of ginger supplements; counsel to avoid concurrent use with other anticoagulants

avoid_supplements.name: Feverfew
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits platelet aggregation and thromboxane synthesis; additive antiplatelet effects
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue feverfew supplementation during prasugrel therapy

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric (curcumin)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet properties; potential additive effect at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; moderate dietary use is generally safe

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil >3g/day)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have minor antiplatelet effects; additive risk at high supplemental doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor bleeding risk; doses ≤3g/day typically safe; counsel on signs of hemorrhage

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin E (high-dose >400 IU/day)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet activity at supraphysiologic doses; theoretical additive effect
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for bleeding; restrict to dietary sources or standard supplemental doses ≤400 IU/day

avoid_foods.name: Excessive alcohol
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases bleeding risk through gastric erosion, platelet dysfunction, and potentiation of antiplatelet effects
avoid_foods.action: Counsel to limit alcohol to ≤1 drink/day for women, ≤2 drinks/day for men; avoid binge drinking

caution_foods.name: Cranberry juice (high-volume)
caution_foods.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet properties and potential interaction with CYP450 metabolism
caution_foods.action: Monitor for increased bleeding; moderate consumption (1-2 cups/day) generally acceptable

caution_foods.name: Green tea (high-volume consumption)
caution_foods.mechanism: Contains vitamin K which may theoretically reduce antiplatelet effectiveness; high caffeine may increase bleeding complications
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption recommended; maintain consistent intake and monitor efficacy

monitoring_notes: Monitor patients for signs of bleeding (petechiae, ecchymosis, GI bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage) as prasugrel carries a Black Box warning for bleeding risk. Assess adherence and educate on medication necessity despite bleeding concerns, as premature discontinuation increases stent thrombosis and acute coronary syndrome risk.
